instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.62(10) defines lobbying as attempting to influence legislative or administrative action by oral or written communication, including preparation time and appearances at public hearings or meetings or service on a committee.

instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.62(11) defines lobbyist as an individual employed by or contracting with a principal (covering professional consultants and in-house lobbyists); §13.62(12) defines principals broadly (associations, corporations, etc.); and §13.695(1) requires state agencies to file statements identifying employees who lobby.
The definitions section §13.62 does not include a definition of "public entity"; it defines "agency" instead, and no separate "public entity" term is defined.

Section 13.621(5) provides an exemption from licensing/registration/reporting for principals who anticipate aggregate lobbying expenditures not exceeding $500 in a calendar year, and §13.64(1) sets a $500 threshold for principal registration — both materiality-based thresholds.

Section 13.62(10) defines lobbying as communications with elective state officials, agency officials, or legislative employees; §13.62(6) defines elective state official to include those holding elective state office (which per §13.62(11p) includes the governor); and §13.62(8) includes the governor's approval/veto as legislative action.

Section 13.62(10) covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative employees; §13.62(3) defines agency officials to include members/officers/employees/consultants participating in administrative action; §13.62(8m) defines legislative employees broadly — covering legislative and executive branches and staff.

Section 13.62(10) includes communications with elective state officials and agency officials; §13.62(11p) lists governor among partisan elective state offices — so lobbying definition covers both legislators and executive officials including the governor.
Section 13.62(10) defines lobbying to include communications with elective state officials and agency officials, and §13.62(11p) confirms the governor is an elective state official.
Section 13.62(10) defines lobbying as communications with elective state officials, agency officials, or legislative employees, which per §13.62(11p) includes the governor.

Lobbying targets defined in §13.62(10) include elective state officials (legislators, governor — §13.62(11p)), agency officials (executive branch members/officers/employees — §13.62(3)), and legislative employees (§13.62(8m)).

Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees from the registration/licensing/reporting requirements when acting in an official capacity, so they are not required to register as lobbyists.

Section 13.62(11) sets compensation ("economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses") and time/frequency ("lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period") standards for who qualifies as a lobbyist; §13.68(1)(a) sets a 10-hour threshold for employee lobbying disclosures.
The lobbyist/principal definitions in §13.62 rely on the employment/compensation relationship and lobbying activity, not on any public charter or special government protection status.
The definitions in §13.62 of lobbyist and principal are based on employment/contracting relationships and lobbying activity, not on ownership criteria.
The definitions in §13.62 do not rely on the structure or composition of revenue; they rely on the employment/compensation relationship and lobbying activity thresholds.
